subtype: Letting go of an imagined future [Response]
passage:
Saturday, 10 pm.
The list came out today. I'm not in the top ten for the architecture course. I've pictured myself at a drafting board since I was fourteen. I cried on the terrace until my head ached. Trisha came up with two mugs and didn't say anything clever, which I was grateful for.
Tonight I let myself grieve the whole life I'd drawn: the studio, the model-making, the city I would move to. It's gone, and that's real. Trisha said the geography department has a mapping workshop on Monday. I said maybe. I don't want to want it. But I looked up the syllabus, and one paragraph about how cities grow made me read it twice.
— Madhuri

qa.q: What did Trisha bring up to the terrace?
qa.a: Trisha came up with two mugs.

qa.q: What was Madhuri feeling on the terrace and that night?
qa.a: Madhuri was grieving the imagined life, the studio, the model-making and the city, with real sadness.

qa.q: What small step could Madhuri take on Monday?
qa.a: Madhuri could go to the mapping workshop, just to look, with no pressure to decide anything.

qa.q: How might Trisha have felt watching Madhuri cry?
qa.a: Trisha was probably caring and unsure what to say, so Trisha brought mugs and stayed, without saying anything clever.

grounding: A student who missed a dream course mourns the life imagined, then slowly builds interest in the available path.

Leela: got the letter. no film school
Devika: oh Leela. I'm so sorry
Leela: I keep imagining the set I was going to be on
Devika: that was a real dream, of course you're gutted
Leela: I'm allowed to be sad for a bit right
Devika: of course. take as long as you need
Leela: the sound design diploma at the polytechnic sent a mail too. I haven't opened it
Devika: no pressure
Two days later
Leela: I opened it. they have a workshop where you make footsteps from gravel and celery. weirdly want to go
Devika: I'll come with you

qa.a: Leela had not opened the mail from the sound design diploma.

qa.q: What did Devika do that made room for Leela to change direction later?
qa.a: Devika accepted the grief without pushing, said take as long as you need and offered to come to the workshop when Leela felt curious.

qa.q: How might Devika have felt when Leela said the workshop weirdly tempted Leela?
qa.a: Devika was probably glad and relieved, offering to come along. Devika had waited without pushing.
